new_issue.body:
## Blocked modeling use

Presto needs an independently trained observation-response module to combine with processing/yield, clearance and downstream pMHC selection. Captured-peptide intensities cannot identify these components by themselves. The current MAPP experiment has repeatable baseline captured composition but weak run-to-run treatment changes; 30 regularized exact/REINFORCE fits fail to beat uniform on the development test. This is motivation to qualify calibration data, not proof that MS response caused the failure.

Search of current Hitlist sources/catalog and issues found no PXD004886 or general known-load peptide response source generation. Existing `calibration_id` / `calibration_applicability` fields and PXD017407 selected-target copies/cell contract should be reused where applicable; they are not yet a materialized non-MHC peptide-response calibration corpus.

## Concrete candidate to qualify

[Collins et al., Nature Communications 2017](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-017-00249-5), deposit **PXD004886**, reports 30 isotope-labeled peptide standards diluted into HEK293 digest, measured at 11 sites. Five dilution levels and repeated acquisitions provide a possible known-load/response anchor. Peptides were assigned to concentration groups using measured response, so group assignment is outcome-informed. The paper reports peak areas and dilution curves in Supplementary Data 4/8, with peptide/sample design in Data 1/2. Low-end points failing quantification criteria were removed; high-load saturation also occurs. Those selection and censoring details must survive curation. This is a candidate identified from the primary publication; file availability, exact joins and calibration quality have not yet been independently verified.

## Requested shared data and metadata

- Pin original publication supplements, repository assets, license/access status, checksums and exact source rows/cells. Resolve peptide × dilution × acquisition × site/day/replicate through source-backed identities; unknown mappings remain unknown.
- Keep actual peptide form, isotope labels/modifications, charge, transitions and integration method separate from canonical sequence. Preserve standard lot, purity, assigned concentration, assignment method and uncertainty when supplied; missing purity is not certified molarity.
- Store nominal loaded amount, concentration, injection volume and units as different quantities with derivation links. Distinguish peptide spiking after digestion from protein spiking before digestion; background digest/enzyme and matrix are protocol context, not evidence that the synthetic standard underwent proteolysis.
- Preserve instrument, acquisition mode, LC/gradient, lab, run order, normalization coefficients and raw versus normalized response. Represent response curves, dilution groups, calibration applicability, quantification limits, saturation, manual integration and exclusions explicitly.
- Recover the intended query/standard universe and all recoverable failed/below-limit observations. An omitted curve point is not a measured zero or a biological negative. Keep identification confidence and quantification eligibility distinct.
- Expose the generation through the same typed evidence/catalog/query/recipe APIs as #737/#746/#739. No Presto-only workbook adapter or parallel metadata system.

## Acceptance and scope

1. Independent conservation/arithmetic checks reproduce source amounts, response values and normalization; discrepancies stay visible. Publish inventory, coverage and per-row dispositions even if qualification fails.
2. A recipe can request non-MHC known-load peptide observations, select raw/normalized endpoints, and explicitly handle censoring and saturation. Provenance reaches every target and context field.
3. Provide split/group constraints for peptide identity, standard lot/preparation and acquisition/site. Repeated injections are not independent biological or peptide generalization examples. Thirty selected standards can anchor a calibration diagnostic; they do not establish broad sequence generalization or transfer from SWATH to MAPP/immunopeptidomics.
4. Document which response parameters are identifiable and what remains confounded. Do not relabel calibrated instrument response as intracellular concentration, digestion yield or MHC capture efficiency.

Related: #757 owns precursor estimates and MAPP specimen/run links; #759 owns controlled processing perturbation/known-substrate panels. This request supplies an independent observation-model anchor, not those biological outcomes. Presto architecture/availability work: pirl-unc/presto#132.
